segments.text: Oh, Captain, My Captain by Walt Whitman
O captain, my captain, our fearful trip is done.
The ship has weathered every wrack, the prize we sought is won.
The port is near, the bells I hear, the people all exulting.
Well follow, eyes, the steady keel, the vessel grim and daring.
But, O heart, heart, heart, O the bleeding drops of red, whereon the deck my captain lies.
O Captain, my Captain, Rise up and hear the bells.
Rise up, for you the flag is flung, For you the bugle trills, For you bouquets and ribbon wreaths, For you the shores are crowding, For you they call the swaying mass, Their eager faces turning.
Here, Captain, dear father, This arm beneath your head,
It is some dream that on the deck you've fallen cold and dead.
His lips are pale and still.
My father does not feel my arm.
He has no pulse nor will.
The ship is anchored safe and sound, its voyage closed and done.
From fearful trip the victor ship comes in with object won.
Exalt, O shores, and ring, O bells, But I, with mournful tread, Walk the deck, my captain lies, Fallen, cold, and dead.
